Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ August 5, 2021

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on August 5, 2021 via
Zoom. Commissioner Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:03 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Bharat Devlia, Food Services Manager
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Anthony Harris, Recreation Supervisor - Sports
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large

Public Comments

  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the minutes from July 1, 2021.
Commissioner Fragoso seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Denmon, Fragoso, McLemore and Beck
  Nays: None

Staff Report

  Stephanie Maldonado presented a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve a 10-year lease agreement
between the City of Inglewood and Historical Society of Centinela Valley (Society) for use of certain
historical buildings (Centinela Adobe Building, Land Office and Heritage Center), generally known
and described as “The Centinela Adobe” located at 7634 Midfield Avenue, Los Angeles, CA.

  Commissioner Beck asked if there is a financial obligation. If so, are there increases in the
dollar amount over the 10-year agreement. Director Barnes stated there is a $1 annual leasing fee
and cost of utilities. The City’s side averages about $13,000 annually which covers ground
maintenance, operations, utilities including security alarm monitoring services and event support.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ August 5, 2021

These cost may deviate in the event of major maintenance issues. This year with homelessness,
vandalism, theft and break-ins fencing needed to be replaced. This is typical general maintenance
cost, not something the Historical Society would bear. Cost is consistent, slight minor changes may
occur due to changes in salaries. We have been working with the Adobe for more than 60 years.

  Commissioner Beck made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
McLemore seconded. The motion was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, Beck and Denmon
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   The Parks Division has replaced landscaping and added wood fiber at Rogers Park and
  added new plants at North Park.
   The Graffiti Abatement staff assisted with the beautification project at both North and Rogers
  Parks. Staff freshened up Darby Park’s restrooms.
   During the month of July, the city experienced heavy graffiti in District 4 near Darby Dixon
  area. Edward Vincent Park Restrooms continue to be tagged heavily.

  Commissioner Denmon complimented the maintenance crew that maintains Vincent Park.
Commissioner Denmon also commended the new maintenance contractor.

  Anthony Harris gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   The City of Inglewood in collaboration with the Los Angeles Rams offers flag football to youth
  ages five (5) through 12 years old. The league is designed to build community by introducing
  the sport of flag football, focusing on fundamental development, skill progression, learning
  the game and having fun. Registration begins August 6, 2021 using the website site
  www.cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com. The season begins October 9, 2021 and ends
  December 11, 2021. League cost are $34.00 for residents and $39.00 for non-residents.
  Commissioner Beck asked about the location for practice. Mr. Harris stated that both practice
  and games will be held at Vincent Park at Champions Field.
   The department is proud to offer FREE outdoor self-defense classes at Center Park on
  Saturdays. Classes are one (1) hour, from 11:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon. Families are
  encouraged to attend. The minimum age requirement is four (4) years. Classes will begin
  on Saturday, July 31, 2021 and will culminate on August 28, 2021. Pre-registration is
  required. Register online at www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ August 5, 2021

    Zumba Classes are being offered at Rogers Park. There will be two class sessions available:
  6:30 p.m. – 7:30 p.m. on Tuesdays and 9:30 a.m. – 10:30 a.m.
  On Saturdays. The Tuesday class focuses on Zumba fitness while the Saturday class
  concentrates on both Zumba fitness and toning. The cost is $4.00 per class. Reservations
  are required. Reservations can be made at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.
    The Edward Vincent, Jr. Park Swim Complex has experienced a malfunction of the pools
  pump. Currently the department is working with the vendor to repair the unit. Youth swim
  lessons have been cancelled. Adult swim and Parent and Me classes resume because staff
  is able to conduct lessons in our smaller pool. General swim remains open Wednesday
  through Sunday for 1-hour per reservation from 1:00 p.m. – 2:00 p.m. and 2:30 p.m. – 3:30
  p.m.  Reservations  are  required.  Reservations  can  be  made  at
  www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.

  Commissioner McLemore asked how long the pool will be down. Mr. Harris stated currently
there is no estimated time of repair, the vendor is working on locating the actual part needed to repair
the unit, when received we’re anticipating the labor can be completed relatively quickly.
Commissioner Denmon stated all over the country there is a shortage of parts for swimming pools
especially commercial pools, along with a shortage of chlorine. In many cases it’s unlikely they will
be able to get the part in a timely manner. Commissioner Denmon also stated he’s has spoken to
someone who said they had been waiting for a part for a swimming pool for over six (6) months.
Commissioner Beck stated he has heard the same thing and it’s unfortunate. Both Commissioner
Denmon and Commissioner Beck thanked Mr. Harris for his report.

  Bharat Devlia gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Senior Center Classes and Activities: The Inglewood Senior Center reopened on July 19,
  2021 with limited activities and programs including Tai Chi, Chair Exercise, Yoga, Knitting,
  and Crochet. The Billiards Room, Gym and Computer Lab are also open. All classes and
  activities are limited in numbers to adhere to safe physical distancing and all who attend
  must wear their mask while inside the Senior Center. Since the soft opening staff has been
  managing the classes with friendly and welcoming demeanors. We look forward to opening
  our doors to full capacity eventually. Staff continues to fill calls and provide assistance during
  these challenging times.
   The Summer Food Summer Program (SFSP) is in full swing, in the month of July, a total of
  5,149 meals were served at our seven (7) locations:
  1. Ash wood Park
  2. Edward Vincent, Jr. Park
  3. Crenshaw-Imperial Library
  4. Darby Park
  5. Rogers Park
  6. Lock haven Community Center
  7. Siminski Park

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ August 5, 2021

    Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Transportation Program continues to provide
  transportation for doctor’s appointments and critical appointments such as dialysis. Drivers
  and passengers continue to wear face mask while practicing safe social distancing during
  transport. Drivers have also been scheduled to transport our seniors and disabled persons
  to other needed appointments. More recently we have been assisting Inglewood Police
  Department by transporting officers to/from SoFi Stadium for events on Saturday’s. We have
  also been transporting minimal participants who are attending limited classes since the soft
  opening at the Senior Center.
    Nutrition: Our Elderly Nutrition program continues to serve fresh cooked meals to
  approximately 350 program participants serving 9,500 meals in July. A total of 2,450 meals
  per week. Our staff are continuing to show their commitment and hard work to the community
  and our seniors during COVID times. The program successfully passed its annual program
  audit with no findings. Our nutrition program continues to run well and received
  commendation from County for the City’s hard work during the pandemic in providing our
  services to the seniors.

Director’s Business

  Sabrina Barnes gave an update regarding the following:
    Capital Improvement Projects: next week staff will be going out to bid for the Vincent Park
  Restroom Construction for the restrooms near the Amphitheater and picnic area. The goal
  is to receive approval from the City Council by September 28,, 2021. This will be one (1) of
  the two (2) restroom projects expected to be reconstructed within this coming year. In the
  next fiscal year, we expect to receive approval for the reconstruction of another set of
  restrooms at Vincent Park consisting of ground up reconstruction. Also anticipate seeing
  major funding and investments for Vincent Park, as it is our regional signature park for the
  community. Funds will go towards upgrades such as the ball fields, fencing, and upgrading
  picnic arbors and playground surfaces. Gopher abatement and other issues are being
  looked into to assist with elevating the park.
    Measure A: the city will be investing both its general funds and Measure A funding in the
  amount of $1.5 million. Originally we discussed having our Measure A Community
  Engagement meeting today, however we did not receive the County’s approval to proceed.
  We anticipate holding the meeting during the Commission’s September meeting. The
  Community Engagement Meeting is meant to have the Community weigh in on projects they
  believe are vitally important and assist in helping the city set its priorities.

  Commissioner Fragoso asked if we previously had a set of capital projects. Director Barnes
answered yes, stating - this portion of the recording was not audible.

  Commissioner Denmon requested a copy of the list to review projects that were completed.
Director Barnes will provide the Commissioners with the Measure A report that will list the
recommended projects in the order of priority.

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ August 5, 2021

  Sabrina Barnes provide information for the following upcoming beautification projects:
    One Day LA Experience: members from Faithful Central Bible Church participated in a
  volunteer service project at Rogers Park. They painted, planted and cleaned-up. It was a
  great day for some improvements and exposure to a potential partnership that may continue.
  Volunteers committed to making this and annual or more frequent project/event.
    National Football League (NFL): with the Super Bowl right around the corner, we have been
  contacted by the NFL’s Green Project expressing interest in doing projects here in
  Inglewood. On September 18, 2021, volunteers with the NFL and Hollywood Park will host
  a beautification project along Hillcrest Boulevard beautifying the center medians.
    Grants: staff applied for two (2) greening project grants and were notified that we have
  secured the grants allowing us to refresh the Community Garden located at Queen Park as
  well as some planting. The second grant we were awarded is The Golden Shovel Project
  which allows the city that previously hosted the Super Bowl (in this case the Tampa City
  Buccaneers) an opportunity to hand a golden shovel to this year’s hosting city. In recognition
  of the 56th Annual Super Bowl, 56 trees will be planted at Vincent Park. We hope to engage
  100 to 150 volunteers on a Saturday to assist in the tree planting.
    Hispanic Heritage Event: Save the date! Planning is underway for the city’s Annual Hispanic
  Heritage Festival on October 2, 2021. The department is taking it day by day with no
  expectation of another shutdown. More information to follow.

  Commissioner Fragoso inquired about the volunteers needed. Director Barnes stated NFL
Projects are expected to consist primarily of NFL staff, possibly players and/or cheerleaders, if
needed, a supplement of general community volunteers. She believes a minimum of 125 to 150
volunteers are needed to assist with the tree planting as well as other needs being taken care of that
day. The NFL Green Project is a collaboration with Hollywood Park that is a project initiated for their
employees to support the City but will also include community volunteers. Commissioner Beck stated
he will be the first volunteer to sign up to plant trees and is also sure the other Commissioners will
as well.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners Comments

  Commissioner Beck stated that the seniors are such an imperative group to the City of
Inglewood. He asked if staff is seeing an increase in numbers now that the Senior Center has re-
opened stating the Senior Center has been such a pillar in the community for many years. Baz Devlia
stated the seniors are still being very cautious and the number of seniors visiting the center are
perfect for the center first opening phase, ensuring that the center is not taking any unnecessary
risks. Safety for everyone is our concern. Sabrina Barnes stated that a limit was placed on how many
seniors are able to visit the Senior Center while also adhering to social distancing protocols. We are

  5
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES ‐ August 5, 2021

taking every precaution to ensure the seniors are comfortable and safe. Commissioner Beck
acknowledged and stated his appreciation for staff’s hard work. The number of reported meals
served is astonishing.

  Commissioner Brown acknowledged the hard work and thanked all of the Department’s staff.

  Commissioner Denmon stated when he reports any complaints, they are addressed
immediately and thanked Director Barnes on her persistence and continued efforts

With no further comments the meeting was adjourned at 6:38 p.m.
